title: A Songbook for the Tide
premise: When pastry chef Edmund Iversen and marine biologist Wren Calloway discover they are co-inheritors of a failing orchard on a tidal island, their rivalry over the deed becomes a reluctant partnership to save both the land and Edmund's drowning café. As the last ferry of the season approaches, they uncover why Edmund's grandmother and Wren's grandfather severed their friendship decades ago — a betrayal of loyalty that mirrors the secrets each is keeping from the other. Forced to choose between selling the orchard to a developer who could rescue his café and protecting the community that has become Wren's found family, Edmund must finally let his guarded heart be trained by something gentler than discipline. They keep the orchard together, forgive the people in their mirrors, and board the last ferry side by side — not leaving, but returning.
about_author: Jude Reyes spent seven years working seasonal jobs on coastal islands before turning those borrowed communities into fiction. They write love stories about stubborn people learning that duty and tenderness can share a table.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. In his struggling café, Edmund rehearses his creed — the heart is trainable muscle — while a bank letter goes unopened. A solicitor's call names him in an inheritance he never expected. Emotional beat: brittle control cracking at the edges.

chapters.title: The Deed With Two Names
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Marine biologist Wren returns to Saltmere Island for her grandfather's funeral and learns he left half of Bramble Orchard to a stranger named Iversen. Emotional beat: grief tangled with betrayal at a dead man's choices.

chapters.title: First Ferry Out
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund crosses to the island intending to sell immediately, but the ferry schedule, the tide charts, and one sharp-tongued biologist conspire against speed. He and Wren meet badly over a disputed gate. Emotional beat: instant friction masking curiosity.

chapters.title: Bramble and Salt
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Walking the overgrown orchard, they find evidence someone tended it secretly for years. Wren claims local knowledge; Edmund claims legal right; neither will budge. Emotional beat: grudging respect planted like a seed.

chapters.title: The Developer's Offer
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. A developer offers enough for Edmund's half to erase his debt entirely. Wren begs for thirty days until the season's last ferry brings the island cooperative's counter-offer. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a reasonable face.

chapters.title: Thirty Days
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren proposes a bargain: she'll help him bake for the island's harvest festival to earn goodwill and money if he delays signing. He agrees, telling himself it's strategy. Emotional beat: a truce neither trusts.

chapters.title: Flour on Her Sleeves
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Baking lessons in the orchard's old kitchen go hilariously wrong; Wren is hopeless and unashamed, and Edmund laughs for the first time in a year. Emotional beat: the heart disobeying its training.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Low tide reveals a sealed tin in the sea wall: letters between their grandparents, once inseparable friends. The final letter is torn in half. Emotional beat: history insisting on being heard.

chapters.title: Found Family, Borrowed Tables
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Festival prep draws them into the island's orbit — Mrs. Okonkwo's jam stall, the ferryman's kids, Wren's chosen family who adopt Edmund suspiciously then completely. Emotional beat: belonging arriving uninvited.

chapters.title: The Half Letter
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund secretly reads his half of the recovered letters and learns his grandmother ended the friendship to protect a secret — possibly about the orchard's ownership. He says nothing. Emotional beat: loyalty curdling into concealment.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A storm damages the orchard walls and threatens the festival; the whole island turns out, Edmund working beside Wren until dawn. Soaked and laughing, they nearly kiss. Emotional beat: desire outrunning denial.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The almost-kiss haunts Edmund; he retreats into work and cold politeness, terrified of wanting anything he can't control. Wren notices the wall going back up. Emotional beat: self-sabotage as self-protection.

chapters.title: The Cooperative's Number
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The island's counter-offer arrives — honest but far below the developer's figure. Wren realizes Edmund's café may not survive either choice, and hates that she cares this much. Emotional beat: love recognizing its own cost.

chapters.title: Confession at Low Water
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. On the tidal flats, truths spill: Edmund admits the developer's offer would save him; Wren admits she'd already asked the cooperative to lowball him, hoping he'd leave. Both wounded, both understood. Emotional beat: honesty as first intimacy.

chapters.title: Harvest Day
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The festival succeeds beyond hope; Edmund's pastries sell out, and islanders quietly pass a hat for his café. For one golden afternoon, everything holds. Emotional beat: joy earned collectively.

chapters.title: The Other Half
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren finds the missing half-letter hidden in her grandfather's boat: the grandparents were partners in love as well as land, parted by a lie one of them told to 'protect' the other. She confronts Edmund about his silence. Emotional beat: betrayal repeating across generations.

chapters.title: Signed, Sealed, Sold
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Humiliated and cornered, Edmund signs the developer's contract at the mainland office — then sits in his car unable to drive away, hearing Wren's voice about what the orchard means. Emotional beat: the moment before the turn.

chapters.title: Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren prepares to winter alone on the island, telling herself she's fine, mirroring every lonely choice her grandfather made. She finds Edmund waiting at the dock, contract torn in two. Emotional beat: the grand gesture done quietly.

chapters.title: Forgiving the Mirror
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. In the old kitchen, each confesses the person they've truly been protecting themselves from: Edmund's fear of needing anyone, Wren's fear of being left. Forgiveness begins with themselves, out loud. Emotional beat: vulnerability as climax.

chapters.title: A Way Through Winter
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Practical magic: Edmund will run a winter pop-up café in the orchard barn; Wren's research grant covers restoration; the cooperative buys the developer out using festival funds and an anonymous check signed 'I.O.' Emotional beat: hope with a business plan.

chapters.title: First Frost, First Kiss
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Planting bare-root saplings for spring, hands in the same hole, they finally kiss among the frost-bitten rows. The heart, Edmund admits, was never a muscle you contain. Emotional beat: tenderness after surrender.

chapters.title: Return Passage
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Spring: the last ferry of the season arrives carrying tourists instead of taking residents away. Edmund and Wren stand on the dock not to leave but to welcome, the songbook of letters open between them. Emotional beat: homecoming as resolution.
